title.narrative: Capacity Building Programme on Social Accountability and Social Activism (Youth Act)

description.narrative: GENERAL OBJECTIVE: To promote social accountability and the safe participation of young activists in democratic life and in the fight against corruption, promoting a culture of transparency and accountability.SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES: 1- Train young activists in Latin America in democratic culture and in research and social auditing methodologies, with a practical and advocacy approach, so that they can demand accountability and safely influence public affairs in their communities.2. Promote the exchange of experiences, interaction and collaboration among young activists committed to public life, transparency and accountability, by supporting them in their research and using educational tools that allow them to transfer the knowledge they have learned to their peers or partners in their communities.MAIN ACTIVITIES Each training in social auditing will be a free training course consisting of three online workshops and a face-to-face meeting, at least one of which will be held at the Spanish Cooperation Training Centre in Santa Cruz (CFSCZ).Each Training will have a total duration of approximately 100 hours, and will be taught by Transparency International with the support of professors from the Complutense University of Madrid (UCM). The latter will teach approximately 30 hours of the total itinerary.The overall approach to the training will be practical so that, with the skills learned, young people can implement research, demand accountability and put into practice advocacy strategies in their municipalities, communities or neighbourhoods in a safe manner. Young people will have specialised mentoring at key moments of the training process and afterwards so that, once the training has finished, they can successfully implement their research.The training will last approximately 5 months, with each workshop taking place over four/five weeks. The modules will be a combination of synchronous and asynchronous sessions. As part of the training itinerary, participants are expected to carry out practical work at home, which will count as part of the training.The online training workshops will be held on the Intercoonecta platform and will cover the following topics: 1) theoretical bases of democracy, participation, human rights and the fight against corruption and case studies, 2) research methodologies and social auditing and 3) advocacy strategies and strategic communication.The workshops will include theoretical presentations, technical tutorials, practical workshops and inspiring masterclasses, as well as other dynamic and innovative methodologies. They will feature the participation of regionally and globally recognized professors, experts and activists from the Complutense University of Madrid, the global network of Transparency International and other relevant institutions.Throughout the training communities of practice will be formed, grouped by themes selected based on the research and projects of the young people, in order to facilitate discussions and exchanges. Among the practical work that the young participants will carry out, it is planned to implement a standardized virtual survey for their peers about their experience with democracy and the impact of the lack of transparency in key areas of community life. This task will serve to articulate the first and second workshops and its results will be condensed into a document that can be published at the end of the two editions of the training itinerary.In both face-to-face meetings, the young participants will be able to deepen the application of the knowledge learned virtually to their specific cases, in a practical way and with the support of tutors. The methodological design of the meeting will take into account the communities of practice created in the virtual phase, so that participants can exchange and implement relevant tools for their research, as well as bring others to the table. In turn, the meeting will provide “trainer of trainers” content so that participants can multiply the scope of the action after the training. The face-to-face meetings will be essential to strengthen the communities of practice and the creation of a network of young social auditors that promotes the exchange of experiences, interaction and collaboration between young people from different Latin American countries committed to public life and the fight against corruption in their communities.COUNTRIES INVOLVED ARE:Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Peru, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Venezuela, Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras, Guatemala, Mexico, Dominican Republic. Value of the contract •Total budget: 296,690 euros•AECID budget: 275,000 euros•Transparency International budget: 21,690 euros
